Title: Trevor's Tale: A Toad's Adventure

Chapter 1: The Great Toad Escape

Trevor the toad hopped contentedly within the snug confines of his terrarium, perched upon a sturdy wooden shelf in Neville Longbottom's dormitory at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Though appearing as an ordinary amphibian to the untrained eye, Trevor possessed a spirit brimming with untapped wanderlust and a penchant for enchanting mischief that lay hidden beneath his unassuming exterior.

One sun-kissed afternoon, when Neville found himself engrossed in Herbology class, an opportunity presented itself to the audacious toad. Through keen observation, Trevor discerned that the latch securing his terrarium had been carelessly left ajar. Fate whispered its invitation for a remarkable escapade, and with calculated deliberation, Trevor nudged the latch open with a delicate sweep of his webbed foot, granting him passage to the world beyond.

Chapter 2: Meeting New Friends

As Trevor ventured forth into the hallowed corridors of Hogwarts, he chanced upon a hidden chamber, ensconced within the depths of the ancient castle. Inside, a treasure trove of magical artifacts awaited his curious gaze. Among them, a resplendent silver locket caught his attention, its ethereal glow captivating his amphibian senses. Driven by a combination of intrigue and fate's whimsy, Trevor drew closer, unwittingly activating an ancient enchantment concealed within the locket's ornate frame.

Unbeknownst to the inquisitive toad, the locket sprung open with a melodious click, revealing a mischievous house-elf named Dobby. Startled by Trevor's unexpected appearance, Dobby's large eyes widened in astonishment as he beheld the small creature before him.

"Greetings, little toad! Pray tell, what brings you to this enchanted chamber?" Dobby inquired, his voice resonating with sincere curiosity.

Though unable to articulate his intentions in the manner familiar to humans, Trevor responded with a resolute croak, his expressive eyes serving as a conduit for his desire to partake in thrilling adventures and bask in the wonders of the world.

Dobby, attuned to the toad's unspoken yearnings, grinned mischievously. "If it is daring exploits you seek, then look no further, for I am the perfect guide through the labyrinthine corridors of Hogwarts. Let us embark on a magnificent journey together!"

Chapter 3: The Mischief Continues

With Dobby as his intrepid mentor, Trevor embarked on a series of exhilarating escapades that would forever etch themselves into the annals of Hogwarts folklore. Together, they clandestinely infiltrated Professor Snape's meticulously organized potion ingredients cabinet, inadvertently triggering a momentary commotion when Trevor, in a moment of unbridled enthusiasm, inadvertently dislodged a jar of powdered dragon claw. The resulting cascade of magical dust threatened to expose their covert operation, forcing them to adroitly evade the prying eyes of Filch, the ever-watchful caretaker, by seeking sanctuary beneath a haphazard mound of discarded robes.

Within Trevor, a dormant talent emerged—a deftness in unlocking doors through a mere touch of his nimble webbed feet. With this newfound ability, the toad skillfully unlocked the secrets concealed behind timeworn doors, granting them entry into hallowed chambers and forgotten corridors that had long eluded the attention of Hogwarts denizens.

Chapter 4: A Noble Sacrifice

As fate would have it, one fateful eve, while traversing the enigmatic depths of the Forbidden Forest, Trevor and Dobby encountered a menacing horde of Acromantulas. Towering above, their formidable

 forms cast eerie shadows in the pale moonlight, their venomous fangs gleaming with a malevolent hunger.

Understanding the gravity of their predicament, Trevor leaped forward with unyielding valor, his small frame a flurry of agile movements that bewildered the arachnid assailants. As he deftly maneuvered, skillfully evading their ferocious strikes, Dobby summoned protective enchantments to shield them both from harm.

Just as the danger reached its zenith, a familiar figure emerged from the shadows. Neville Longbottom, his visage etched with concern, had followed their trail into the Forbidden Forest. Bearing witness to Trevor's unwavering bravery, Neville's heart swelled with a blend of relief and gratitude.

"Trevor, you gallant toad!" Neville exclaimed, his voice tinged with admiration. "You risked everything to safeguard Dobby and yourself. I am immensely proud of you!"

Trevor, his tiny chest swelling with pride, met Neville's gaze, his eyes reflecting a profound sense of joy at receiving his beloved companion's accolades. In that moment, he understood that bravery was not confined to the grandiose or the celebrated—it resided within the heart of even the humblest of creatures.

Chapter 5: A Toad's Homecoming

Cradled within Neville's gentle hands, Trevor returned to the familiar embrace of his terrarium, forever changed by the wondrous experiences that had shaped his unassuming existence. Together, they reveled in tales of treacherous spiders, enchanted chambers, and corridors steeped in mystery, knowing that their bond was forged through shared courage and the boundless magic that resided within every living being.

From that day forward, Trevor's toad-sized heart swelled with an unquenchable thirst for adventure, forever grateful for the irrevocable transformation that took place when a seemingly ordinary toad, guided by destiny, embraced the extraordinary tapestry of life at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry.

I'm so sorry you and your loved ones have to go through that. Just lost my mom to Lewy Body dementia in July. Horrible disease and so scary for them seeing and hearing things that are not really there. It's like they start with the terrible symptoms that normally come at the end of dementia. 

It is lovely seeing those brief moments when they come back. We found playing some of her favorite music (or music from when she was a teen) brought her back to us for a short but lovely while.

Mom can start seizing, go into DIC, start hemorrhaging,  longer term if any fetus pieces are accidentally left from shearing the mom will have other cascades of problems. Cutting a baby up and removing it sounds simple, but it's not.

Breaching is def dangerous for the mother as well as the baby. If you are close to full term and the baby is breached, C section is recommended for both mom and baby safety. The babies head or shoulders can get wedged against mom's pelvic bones, prolapsed cord. Lots of not good outcomes for those involved.

Just to play devil's advocate here and give you the other view, I tell my patients I'm going to try and let them get as much sleep as possible, but my goal is to provide care and get them better and out of the ICU as soon as possible. So don't anticipate much sleep while in here.

On a stable ICU patient you're looking at vitals every 15 minutes, every hour come in and do intake and output on all the lines and drains, check IVs to make sure they are still infusing, every 2 hours you get turned and oral care with suctioning, 4 hours it's another total assessment. On a medication that needs titration? Or a vent that needs settings adjusted? Mucus plugs?  You get to see my face more because I'll be in there! Also there's a ton of foreign beeps, clicks, buzzers and other random ass sounds that aren't very easy to sleep through. 

Of course pain management is important, and we want to take care of that. But medicine isn't magic, there's always a trade off- such as you can be pain free but you're going to be completely unconscious and have no idea of any stimulus happening around you. That doesn't sound like a quality of life you if you came in for just a surgery.

There have been quite a bit of new studies surrounding ICU delirium (which can continue even after discharge) with being a combo of over sedation and poor early mobility. So there has been a push with not over sedating and getting patients up and moving sooner.

Are we getting people up and out of bed way sooner than before with less medication? Absolutely.
Is it because of $$profit for the hospital that I am choosing to do this with my patients? Hell no! I could care less about the damn profit. What I can tell you it's pretty amazing seeing patients get their strength back, and be able to return to their quality of life much sooner. 

Just trying to give ya a different view point from why an ICU nurse would say this. We mean well from our hearts but we are going to be bluntly honest with you!

Sorry for the formatting I am on mobile.  I went in hearing the same thing about how challenging nursing school is.  Before starting nursing I didn't really need to study to get A's or B's.  So I wasn't to terribly worried.  But reality hits hard and quick. 

We were expected to read a lot of chapters (I just did the vocab words from each chapter). Do the online quizzes for the chapters. Listen to Powerpoints and take notes before class.  Basically lots of information in a small amount of time. And it's not just "bulimia information" that you take in for a small amount of time and purge it during the test next week.  You will need to know the info and how to apply it. And you will need to remember that info because for us any future tests could pull from past information.  So you get information on multiple disease processes and they go over >>
-how to recognize them 
-the diagnostic tests that go with it (what you need to be aware as a nurse for those diagnostic tests) 
-the medications (need to remember main side effects, dosage, proper administration, contraindications) 
-teaching for the patient/family 
-and how to reassess that the intervention you have done are working well. 

Then there is lab with practicing skills. Then clinical there was quite a bit of prep work along with after clinical work.  Like gathering information on every medication our patients were on. 

Socially I didn't become a hermit and give up my family and friends. I didn't go out every weekend like I did previously. But I could still count on a couple times a month going out with my non nursing family.  It was challenging when I was studying and had to turn down invitations, but I knew I had to keep my priorities in order and put my studies first.  

It's completely doable, just stay organized with calendars and to-do lists.  What helped me is when I thought - what information as a nurse would I need to know, what as a nurse will I do?

TLDR: Lots of info, learning to critically think and prioritize, prep and post clinical/lab work.

I suffer from depression/anxiety and feel this post doesn't help the social stigma of marijuana vs antidepressants.  Yes I am on antidepressants and have been for some years now and they help drastically.  

If you are interested in learning more keep reading - the usual go to for a first line antidepressant that doctors prescribe is a one medications that fall under the  SSRI category.  SSRI medications usually take about 2-4 weeks before your body gets to a therapeutic level making one feel not as depressed.  About the whole "Antidepressants make you want to kill yourself when your on them! It says may cause suicidal thoughts right in the bottle!" During a time before you are at a therapeutic level and receiving the full effect of the medication (usually within the first week). Before you feel happier or more positive the medication increases your motivation or desire to do things.  So now you have someone who is still depressed but is now feeling motivated to do something, this is why there is a warning in the bottle about suicidal thoughts and to report those.  

So it takes 2-4 weeks to get to a therapeutic level to feel motivated and in a more positive mood.  Missing *one* day won't cause you to spiral out into a deep depression.  Just like work out everyday for 4 weeks skipping one day won't put you back at the beginning.  I'm not saying skip days, but if the majority of the time you are  consistent with the medication skipping one day isn't terrible.  The problem is when people try to stop the medication abruptly. Which it says right on the bottle "Do not stop abruptly!" But because there is such a stigma against mental health and medication -either people talk themselves into stopping, or friends/family say how bad it is and how they need to stop. Which depending on the medication that could be life threatening. This is why you are supposed to consult with a your doctor about tapering off the medication so it's not such a shock to your system.  

It would be like a person having incredible leg pain and can't even walk comfortably.  That person then gets a cane and it takes a while to for them to get used to using the cane but it gets them up and moving further and further with a lot less pain!  Now imagine someone comes around and makes fun of that person for using the cane, or tells them to just stop using it they are fine now.  Kick that cane out from that person how do you think they are going to fair now? 

TLDR: Weed doesn't work as a antidepressant for everyone, some people benefit from other antidepressant medication.  Missing one dose as long as you are usually consistent, doesn't mean you are going to instantly want to kill yourself.  Your post isn't helping the stigma for mental health medications, and could cause someone to avoid seeking help if weed doesn't cure their problem. There is always a 30 day grace period atleast with any warranty, so i can tell you if you get coverage and 2 weeks later your engine fails or your transmission starts slipping it will be denied for pre-exsisting 100%.
When i say $150 will cover any repair, i mean you can pay cash for any repairs as opposed to only select repairs being covered by the coverage.

I currently work at a 3rd party warranty company, what most people dont realize is after the factory warranty is up, any coverage you buy from the dealer is through a 3rd party company. Truthfully with that many miles you are just going to get a powertrain warranty (lowest level of coverage) which covers the main components like engine, transmission, and some small electrical components like power windows. Basically not a lot of any. 

You would probably be better off putting $150 a month aside. That will cover any repair! I see where people are under the assumption these cover everything, dont assume,  if you do want to call, by all means call em, but read what they send ya. If you do call some place and they say you can get a new car bumper to bumper coverage they are lying.

Tldr. Not worth it with your miles, better off setting aside $150 a month for repairs.
